title: Enterprise RAG Implementation: Ingestion Worker, Pgvector & Hybrid Pipeline
description: Implement the end-to-end RAG system in .NET 9: background document ingestion worker, token-aware chunking, batched vector embeddings with Microsoft.Extensions.AI, and hybrid BM25 + pgvector query execution.

data.text: Document ingestion in the enterprise must never run synchronously within the HTTP request thread. Ingesting multi-megabyte PDFs, Word documents, or internal wiki dumps requires document parsing, recursive chunking, token counting, batched embedding generation, and database indexing. If handled synchronously, requests time out and resource spikes degrade the chat API. EnterpriseNexus implements an asynchronous ingestion pipeline using .NET 9 `BackgroundService` and bounded `System.Threading.Channels`.

data.caption: Asynchronous Document Ingestion and Indexing Pipeline
data.code:
flowchart LR
    A[Document Upload API] -->|Push Job| B[Bounded Channel Queue]
    B -->|Pull Job| C[Ingestion Background Worker]
    C --> D[Document Extraction: PDF / Markdown / Office]
    D --> E[Recursive Chunking: 400 Tokens, 50 Overlap]
    E --> F[Batched Embedding: Microsoft.Extensions.AI (Batch=16)]
    F --> G[(PostgreSQL pgvector / HNSW + GIN Full-Text Index)]
    G --> H[Update Document Status: Indexed & Searchable]

data.text: This worker processes documents asynchronously with concurrency control, backpressure handling, and graceful shutdown.

data.title: DocumentIngestionWorker.cs in .NET 9
data.content: Consuming from a bounded channel, generating embeddings with IEmbeddingGenerator, and persisting to pgvector.

data.text: At query time, the hybrid search service executes the vector similarity query and full-text keyword search in parallel, then fuses the results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

data.title: PostgresHybridSearchService.cs
data.content: Executing concurrent vector and lexical queries against PostgreSQL with pgvector, followed by in-memory RRF fusion.

data.title: Batched Embedding Generation
data.content: Never generate embeddings in a one-by-one loop (`foreach { await GenerateAsync() }`). OpenAI and Azure OpenAI endpoints incur significant HTTP overhead per call. Always batch chunks in arrays of 16 to 64 items to maximize throughput and minimize latency.

data.title: RAG Implementation Verification Checklist
items: Ingestion offloaded to BackgroundService consuming from bounded System.Threading.Channels
Chunking algorithm preserves paragraph boundaries with 10% token overlap to prevent cutoffs
Embedding calls batched (16-32 chunks per request) with Polly retry policies for rate limits
PostgreSQL pgvector HNSW index configured with cosine distance operator (<=>)
Concurrent execution of vector and BM25 full-text queries via Task.WhenAll
Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges candidate lists deterministically without score distortion

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Asynchronous ingestion workers decouple heavy document parsing from the user-facing web API.
Microsoft.Extensions.AI simplifies batched embedding generation with provider independence.
Hybrid search in PostgreSQL combines pgvector ANN search and full-text ts_rank.
Next, we prepare the infrastructure deployment using Bicep, Azure Container Apps, and GitHub Actions.
data.takeaway: A production RAG implementation is an end-to-end data pipeline: robust ingestion, token-aware chunking, batched embeddings, and hybrid retrieval fusion.
